$description: #271 harvest lane C — DECISION TABLE. ONLY the non-unanimous rules. One row per rule; each system's position is a VERBATIM quote or the word silent. Silence is recorded, not counted as disagreement. Options are for Dave; the recommendation is THIS LANE'S and is not a ruling.
$runbook: knowledge/_RUNBOOK-external-claims.md — every quote is EXTERNAL and carries its source in SOURCES.json.
$silence_note: Spectrum, Atlassian and Fluent 2 are SILENT in every row because their pages are client-rendered and served no guidance text — see SOURCES.json.refused. Their silence is a FETCH FAILURE, not a considered position.

rows.rule: At what point does the primary navigation leave the masthead and become a column?
rows.ours: roles.json: side-nav when "> 7 destinations or two nav levels"; top-nav when "default for dashboards". Axis = DESTINATION COUNT.

positions.USWDS: The basic header is great if you have a modest number of sections
positions.Material 3: Navigation rails let people switch between UI views on mid-sized devices.
positions.Carbon (IBM): Use the left panel if there are more than five secondary navigation items
positions.Apple HIG: a more compact control such as a tab bar may provide a better
positions.NN/g: Vertical navigation is a good fit for broad or growing IAs

rows.why_non_unanimous: Four systems, THREE different axes: a count (Carbon, 5), a vague count (USWDS), device size (M3, Apple), IA shape (NN/g). Our 7 is corroborated by nobody and contradicted in number by Carbon.
options: Keep 7 and record that it is a house number no external system shares.
Move to Carbon's 5, the only other explicit count in the set.
Drop the number: cut on "the destination set does not fit one band at the narrowest supported desktop width", which is measurable and matches USWDS's and NN/g's reasoning.
Add M3's device-size axis as a SECOND gate so the frame is chosen by count on desktop and by breakpoint below it.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 3 — a fit test. It is machine-checkable, it survives a font change, and it explains why every system picked a different number: they were all approximating the same fit.

rows.rule: How many levels of hierarchy may a persistent side navigation show?
rows.ours: roles.json: side-nav when "> 7 destinations or two nav levels" — implies a ceiling of 2.

positions.USWDS: To display a navigational hierarchy with one to three levels.
positions.Carbon (IBM): The left panel does not support three tiers of navigation.
positions.Apple HIG: In general, show no more than two levels of hierarchy in a sidebar.

rows.why_non_unanimous: Same KIND (a depth ceiling), different NUMBER: Carbon 2, Apple 2, USWDS 3. And the two systems that cap at 2 send the overflow to DIFFERENT places — Carbon to in-page Tabs, Apple to a split view.
options: Cap at 2 and route the third tier to app-shell-multi-column (Apple's escape hatch).
Cap at 2 and route the third tier to in-page Tabs (Carbon's escape hatch) — but this collides with R11.
Allow 3 with USWDS and carry no escape hatch.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1 — cap 2, overflow to multi-column. It matches our own roles.json number and does not require ruling tabs legal as navigation.

rows.rule: At what depth do breadcrumbs earn their place?
rows.ours: breadcrumbs.meta.json when: "shape = ancestor-path x links AND depth >= 2".

positions.GOV.UK: Do not use the breadcrumbs component on websites with a flat structure
positions.USWDS: Omit breadcrumbs on the homepage of a site.
positions.Carbon (IBM): a hierarchy of more than two levels
positions.Ant Design: When the system has more than two layers in a hierarchy.
positions.NN/g: Breadcrumbs augment but do not replace those main forms of navigation.

rows.why_non_unanimous: The KIND is unanimous (depth). The NUMBER is not: we say 2, Carbon and Ant both say more than 2 (i.e. 3). GOV.UK, USWDS and NN/g decline to give one. Same shape as the #270 radio→dropdown finding.
options: Keep depth >= 2 — our number, already on the meta.
Move to depth >= 3, matching the only two systems that quantify it.
Carry no number: "the site is not flat AND this is not the home page", following GOV.UK and USWDS.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 2 — depth >= 3. At depth 2 the trail reads Home / Current, which is one link and no orientation; the two systems that bothered to count both landed on 3.

rows.rule: May breadcrumbs and a persistent side navigation appear on the same page?
rows.ours: SILENT. roles.json gives both a when and no not-with. Nothing forbids the pair today.

positions.GOV.UK: consider whether your users need the additional support of breadcrumbs
positions.USWDS: When side navigation is used in combination with main navigation, it may be redundant
positions.Carbon (IBM): should never entirely replace the primary navigation
positions.NN/g: Breadcrumbs augment but do not replace those main forms of navigation.

rows.why_non_unanimous: USWDS and GOV.UK lean AGAINST the pair; NN/g and Carbon treat breadcrumbs as a supplement that co-exists with primary navigation. Genuine split on the same question.
options: Rule the pair legal (NN/g / Carbon position) and say nothing more.
Rule the pair a REVIEWABLE exception: legal only where the side-nav shows one level and the content is deeper than it.
Rule the pair illegal — breadcrumbs only in app-shell-top-nav and app-shell-doormat.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. It is the only reading under which both camps are right, and it is checkable: side-nav levels < content depth.

rows.rule: Where does FILTERING one content set live — Tabs, Segmented-control, or the filter bar?
rows.ours: roles.json: tabs when "local — peer views in one context"; segmented-control (#270 proposal) when "the choice RE-PRESENTS content already on screen". By our own reading a filtered list-view is a re-presentation, so it is SEGMENTED — but our templates ship it as Tabs.

positions.GOV.UK: the first section is more relevant than the others for most users
positions.Material 3: Use tabs to group content into helpful categories.
positions.Carbon (IBM): When toggling between different formats of the same content or filtering the same content
positions.Polaris (Shopify): Represent the same kind of content, such as a list-view with different filters

rows.why_non_unanimous: A three-way conflict on the identical use case. Polaris puts filtered list-views on TABS. Carbon puts filtering on the CONTENT SWITCHER (our Segmented-control) by name. Ant sends the secondary level to a radio-button group. We have a fourth answer available (filter-toolbar-bar) and no rule.
options: Filters go to Segmented-control (Carbon): tabs only where the panels hold DIFFERENT content, never the same content re-filtered.
Filters go to Tabs (Polaris): tabs are the list-view switcher and Segmented-control is reserved for presentation (view, scale, period).
Filters go to filter-toolbar-bar whenever there are more than N filters, with Segmented-control for a single filter of <= 5 values.
Cut on PERSISTENCE: a filter that belongs to the record set is toolbar; one that belongs to the reader's current view is segmented; tabs never filter.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1, with option 4 as the prose. Carbon's line is the only one that names our exact component pair, and it keeps Tabs' meaning single: different content, not the same content re-cut.

rows.rule: Is a Tabs strip inside the page header legal, given three systems say tabs are never navigation?
rows.ours: page-header-lockup.meta.json ships an OPTIONAL Tabs row; template-detail composes it. roles.json: tabs when "local — peer views in one context".

positions.GOV.UK: do not use the tabs component as a form of page navigation
positions.Polaris (Shopify): Not be used for primary navigation.
positions.Ant Design: Card Tabs: for managing too many closeable views.

rows.why_non_unanimous: Three systems forbid tabs as navigation and we already ship them in the page header. Worse, Carbon contradicts ITSELF: its side-nav page says "content to display beneath a sub-menu, use tabs within the page." The prohibition may be about PRIMARY navigation only — Polaris says 'primary', GOV.UK says 'page navigation', Carbon says neither.
options: Rule our header Tabs LEGAL: they switch peer views of one record and are not navigation, which satisfies Polaris's 'primary' wording.
Rule them legal only where each tab does NOT change the URL — a machine-checkable clause.
Rule them illegal and move sub-page routing to a second nav band in app-shell-top-nav.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. It keeps template-detail as built, and turns a vague prohibition into a gate clause a builder can fail.

rows.rule: Does the navigation rail carry a destination count?
rows.ours: roles.json: nav-rail when "dense app, content cannot spare 248px". No count.

positions.Material 3: They can contain 3-7 destinations plus an optional FAB.

rows.why_non_unanimous: Only M3 ships a rail and only M3 gives a number. One source is not consensus, and M3's own axis (device size) differs from ours (content width) — so the number arrives attached to a different rule.
options: Adopt 3–7 with M3.
Carry no count; the rail's rule stays a width rule.
Adopt an upper bound only (<= 7), matching our top-nav's 7.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. It gives the rail a ceiling consistent with R1's family and does not import M3's device-size axis by the back door.

rows.rule: What triggers a mega-footer (doormat) instead of the plain footer?
rows.ours: roles.json: doormat frame when "marketing / servicing site with a mega-footer" — circular, no trigger. footer.meta is the OPERATOR footer, a different object.

positions.GOV.UK: Use the footer at the bottom of every page of your service.
positions.USWDS: Use the big footer when your footer has more than five links.
positions.Polaris (Shopify): Be positioned at the bottom of the interface

rows.why_non_unanimous: USWDS is the only system with a number, and it contradicts itself on WHAT goes in the mat: "Use the big footer when you want to replicate your site's navigation scheme" against "The footer doesn't need to mirror the header." Our antiPattern already forbids the duplication.
options: Adopt ">5 links" as the doormat trigger and keep our no-duplication antiPattern.
Adopt ">5 links" AND allow the mat to repeat the masthead (USWDS's other line) — this would REVERSE our antiPattern[0].
Carry no count; the doormat is chosen by SURFACE (marketing/public) alone.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. The number is free and our antiPattern is the better half of USWDS's own contradiction.

rows.rule: What makes a Back-to-top control appear?
rows.ours: roles.json: back-to-top when "page chrome only". No trigger, no threshold, no cardinality.

positions.Ant Design: For global functionality on the site.
positions.NN/g: Use a Back to Top button for pages that are longer than 4 screens

rows.why_non_unanimous: One quantified source (NN/g, 4 screens) and one unquantified (Ant). Everyone else silent. Our when says nothing about when it appears, which makes it unbuildable.
options: Adopt NN/g wholesale: appears past 4 viewport-heights, one per page, bottom-end, labelled.
Adopt the threshold only and leave placement to the component.
Rule the threshold an implementation detail and keep the when as a role statement.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. It is the only source in the whole slice that gives a complete, testable rule, and our own meta already agrees on the icon-button/secondary-tier treatment.

rows.rule: How long is a "long document" before anchor-nav applies?
rows.ours: anchor-nav roles.json when: "in-page, long document". No threshold.

positions.GOV.UK: a list of links at the start of the page (known as 'anchor links')
positions.USWDS: pages that include three or more distinct content sections
positions.Ant Design: For displaying anchor hyperlinks on page and jumping between them.

rows.why_non_unanimous: USWDS is the only system that quantifies it (3 sections OR 3 viewport heights). GOV.UK endorses anchor links as an accordion alternative but sets no size. Ant states purpose only. One number against two silences.
options: Adopt USWDS's OR-test verbatim: sections >= 3 OR length >= 3 viewport-heights.
Adopt the section count only (>= 3) — viewport heights depend on the reader's window.
Keep "long" unquantified and let review judge it.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. Both halves are measurable at build time and the OR-test catches the two different ways a page gets long.

rows.rule: When does a masthead flyout become a mega-menu?
rows.ours: SILENT. navigations.meta ships a main-nav flyout with no size rule.

positions.USWDS: more than six links in any of your dropdown menus

rows.why_non_unanimous: Single source. Nobody else quantifies it; nobody contradicts it either — so it is single-external rather than consensus.
options: Adopt 6 as the flyout ceiling.
Carry no ceiling.
Tie it to R1's fit test instead of a count.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. It is cheap, it is the only number available, and it stops the flyout quietly becoming an unruled mega-menu.

rows.rule: Is the Hero restricted to unauthenticated marketing surfaces?
rows.ours: SILENT as a predicate. hero.meta says "marketing banner" in prose; roles.json does not list hero in page-title at all.

positions.USWDS: Don't try to include forms or side navigation.

rows.why_non_unanimous: The most obvious rule in the page-title role and nobody writes it down. USWDS's landing-page restraint is the closest external statement and it is about page CONTENTS, not about who may use a hero.
options: Rule Hero legal only where authenticated = false, and add USWDS's no-forms / no-side-nav restraint.
Rule Hero legal on authenticated overview pages too (some banks do this), with the restraint dropped.
Rule Hero out of the page-title role entirely and give it its own marketing role.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. It is the line every one of our shells already assumes, and writing it down is what stops a hero landing on a dashboard.

rows.rule: Does app-shell-split (and Splitter) carry a viewport condition?
rows.ours: roles.json: split frame when "two peers on screen at once"; splitter when "the reader sizes two panes". Neither mentions viewport.

positions.Apple HIG: Prefer using a split view in a regular — not a compact — environment.

rows.why_non_unanimous: Single source, but it names a failure our whens cannot currently prevent: a two-pane frame on a phone. Nobody contradicts Apple; everyone else is silent because nobody else ships a splitter.
options: Add "viewport = regular" to the FRAME's when only.
Add it to both the frame and the Splitter control.
Leave both viewport-agnostic and handle it in the responsive rules instead.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. The frame owns the decision; the Splitter is a control and should stay usable wherever a frame legitimately places it.

rows.rule: Two dashboard templates answer the same question — what discriminates them?
rows.ours: template-dashboard-bento.meta.json, verbatim: it answers the SAME question as Template dashboard and "differs in ONE thing: its layout".
rows.why_non_unanimous: NO EXTERNAL SYSTEM SPEAKS — no public system ships page templates at this granularity (USWDS's five templates map onto none of ours). Non-unanimous against OURSELVES: a role whose axis is 'the question the page answers' cannot discriminate two providers that ask the same question.
options: Make bento a VARIANT of template-dashboard, not a second template.
Keep both and give bento an explicit non-job when: "the brief asks for the bento grammar".
Keep both and re-cut the questions so they differ (e.g. bento = 'how are things across SEVERAL domains at once').
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. Two providers with one question is the defect the role axis exists to prevent; s217-D2/D3 describe a grammar, not a job.

rows.rule: What language and furniture may an error page carry?
rows.ours: template-error.meta: binds no RAG colour, invents no support semantics. Silent on language and on breadcrumbs.

positions.GOV.UK: technical jargon like 404 or bad request
positions.USWDS: Don't use this template for form validation errors, submission errors

rows.why_non_unanimous: Both systems agree on SCOPE (page-level failures only) — that half is unanimous. They diverge on furniture: GOV.UK additionally bans breadcrumbs and humour and red text on a not-found page; USWDS bans none of that and our meta bans only RAG colour.
options: Adopt GOV.UK's bans (no 404 jargon, no breadcrumbs, no humour) as gate clauses.
Adopt them as content guidance only, off the gate.
Adopt the no-breadcrumbs clause only — it is structural and checkable; leave tone to review.
rows.recommendation_THIS_LANES_NOT_RULED: LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. A gate can check for a breadcrumb; it cannot check for humour.
